classification.parent: Grammar > Preposition > Meaning and Pattern Selection
classification.reason: This topic trains learners to choose prepositions by semantic function and fixed grammar patterns.

similarities: All three are related to location and space.
All three are common in everyday English.
All three can be used with places such as room, bag, and box.
differences: Use in for location: The keys are in my bag.
Use into for movement from outside to inside: She ran into the room.
Use inside for stronger contrast with outside: Wait inside the building.
Choose in when you describe a stable position.
Choose into when the verb shows motion.
Choose inside when you want to emphasize the inner area.

association.note: Group prepositions by function: time, place, movement, relationship, and fixed collocation.

example.english: Our result depends on careful preparation.
example.translation: 我们的结果取决于充分准备。
example.note: depends on is a fixed verb plus preposition pattern.

counterExample.reason: interested takes the preposition in, not on. Correct form: She is interested in biology.

scenario.description: Office: We are responsible for the final report. School: I am good at chemistry but weak in history. Travel: We walked into the station at noon. Daily conversation: I did it by mistake, not on purpose. Academic writing: The results depend on sample size. Business email: Please send the file to me by 5 p.m.

conversation.speaker: Lina
conversation.text: Who is responsible for the slides?

conversation.speaker: Kai
conversation.text: Mina is, and I am working on the data section.

conversation.speaker: Lina
conversation.text: Great. Our grade depends on clear structure.

conversation.speaker: Kai
conversation.text: Then let us meet at 4:00 in the library.

mnemonic.content: Ask first: time, place, movement, or fixed phrase? If it is fixed phrase, memorize the pair as one chunk, such as interested in and depend on.

confusion.confusedWith: in vs into; at vs in for time; interested in vs interested on
confusion.reason: Use into when movement crosses a boundary, use in for location, use at for exact clock time, and memorize adjective plus preposition patterns as fixed units.
